question: What is the meaning of digital twin in relation to interactive decision support tools (tools that support exploration and decision-making in ce object governance)?
data_group: interactive decision support tools (tools that support exploration and decision-making in ce object governance)
description: A digital twin is a digital replica of a physical product, building, or system. It provides diverse data, mostly focusing on product performance and technical properties. In the context of circular economy (CE) object governance, digital twins can be used as interactive decision support tools to explore and make decisions about product lifecycle management, including material reuse and recycling. They can help track and trace materials, support product passports, and enable the implementation of international standards for circularity. This allows for more informed decision-making and the development of circular economy metrics.

1. Introduction
Concepts for a circular economy (CE) are being introduced widely in order to assure
supply and use of materials and energy without compromising the needs of future gen-
erations. Digitalization is one tool being studied to implement the CE [1]. Digital twins
are being commonly used to digitally represent physical products [2]. These provide
diverse data, mostly focusing on product performance and technical properties. For ex-
ample, in the construction sector, digital twins for products and building elements are
incorporated into Building Integrated Management (BIM) software as BIM Objects [3,4].
Environmental properties are sometimes added to digital twins for products. One question
arising from this evolution of digital twins is, which types of data do these require in order
to reﬂect circular economy characteristics and metrics? A 2020 United Nations Environment
Program (UNEP) ﬁnancial institutions survey examined this question after extensively
reviewing CE literature and conducting a survey of ﬁnancial institutions.
